In addition, the 16Si-12Zr alloy exhibits a hypereutectic microstructure consisting of primary γ-Nb₅Si₃ and two distinct eutectic morphologies, which is attributed to solidification process modifications caused by increased Si and Zr concentrations.

As demonstrated in Fig. 9 (d), the 10Si-12Zr alloy exhibits extensive crack deflection, bridging, and branching phenomena along the propagation path, accompanied by secondary crack formation, which correlates with its optimal fracture toughness performance.
This propagation behavior facilitates energy dissipation through surface energy conversion, with greater energy consumption corresponding to improved fracture toughness.
Thus, the high-temperature compressive performance of the Nb-30Ti-10Si- y Zr alloys and the Nb-30Ti-13Si- y Zr alloys improves to some extent.
